title: beads_web-374.5: MarkerAwareCtaBlock component + FleetCard integration + tests (E2E)
description:
## Outcome

Add the `MarkerAwareCtaBlock` component (`src/components/fleet/MarkerAwareCtaBlock.tsx`, ~150 lines) and integrate it ADDITIVELY into `FleetCard.tsx` (~25 new lines, no removals). The component renders all three marker-driven visual states from a single switch on `intent.kind`. Integration test runs through `next build` to catch any inadvertent fs/marker-reader imports leaking into the React tree.

## Scope

- In: `MarkerAwareCtaBlock.tsx` (new); FleetCard.tsx (modified ADDITIVELY); component unit tests; FleetCard integration tests.
- Out: per-bead marker reads (out of scope per ADR-006); marker schema changes (covered by sy3d epics); reconciler-side changes (mirror only, do not re-implement); niii.6 "Close Epic" button (sequence after this bead — see plan summary).

## ADR-003: Single component for all three visual states

Render all three marker-driven states from one component via internal `switch (intent.kind)` with TypeScript exhaustive checking (`never` type guard — regression #7). Three rendering branches plus `default` returning `null`. Architect rejected three-separate-components alternative because they share the same hook, intent derivation, and dispatch callback.

### Visual treatments (per architect ADR-007 + bead description)

- `"marker-driven"`: primary CTA button. Label = `intent.action`. Small (10×10 px) inline marker badge before the action text — "compass" or "pin" icon (Heroicons or equivalent). Tooltip = `intent.reason` (e.g., "explicit next_agent field" or "blocker_class=design-question maps to architect").
- `"needs-decision"`: amber-bordered amber-tinted banner styled like `AttentionBanner` (visual precedent — copy the Tailwind classes, do NOT import the component). Surface `intent.blockerMessage` inline. Offer "Run coherence" button → dispatches `run-coherence-agent`.
- `"failure"`: orange/red-tinted banner. Surface `intent.recommendation` text inline. Offer "Re-run <stage>" button → dispatches the same-stage resume action via `intent.action`.
- `"default"`: returns `null` (FleetCard's existing stage-default CTAs render unchanged).

## FleetCard integration (ADDITIVE only)

Add `<MarkerAwareCtaBlock>` invocation above the existing stage-default CTA blocks. NO removals. Existing tests (`FleetCard.attention.test.tsx`) MUST continue passing unmodified.

Reuse `onPipelineAction` callback (existing FleetBoard contract — `PipelineActionPayload` shape). Marker-driven CTAs dispatch action names already valid (`run-coherence-agent`, `run-architect`, etc. — verified against `agent-action-map.ts`).

## Critical: Edge Runtime guarantee

The integration test `FleetCard.marker-aware.test.tsx` MUST run cleanly through `next build` (or equivalent build verification) to catch inadvertent `fs`/`marker-reader` imports leaking into the React tree. Any import path that pulls `fs` into a client component will fail the build (regression beads_web-8wh). The hook (374.4) talks to the route via fetch — the React tree must NOT import `marker-reader.ts` for runtime.

Type-only imports (`import type { MarkerData } from './marker-reader'`) are OK — they erase at compile.

## Acceptance criteria

1. GIVEN `intent.kind = "marker-driven"`, WHEN MarkerAwareCtaBlock renders, THEN a primary CTA button is shown with label = intent.action AND a 10×10 marker badge appears inline before the action text AND tooltip text = intent.reason (per ADR-007).
2. GIVEN `intent.kind = "needs-decision"`, WHEN it renders, THEN an amber-bordered amber-tinted banner is shown AND `intent.blockerMessage` appears inline AND a "Run coherence" button is offered (clicking dispatches `onPipelineAction({ epicId, action: "run-coherence-agent" })`).
3. GIVEN `intent.kind = "failure"`, WHEN it renders, THEN an orange/red-tinted banner is shown AND `intent.recommendation` text appears inline (or a placeholder when null) AND a "Re-run <stage>" button is offered (clicking dispatches `onPipelineAction({ epicId, action: intent.action })`).
4. GIVEN `intent.kind = "default"`, WHEN it renders, THEN the component returns `null` (FleetCard's existing CTAs render unchanged — defends AC #4 of bead description: current behaviour preserved).
5. GIVEN any switch case is added/removed, WHEN TypeScript compiles, THEN exhaustive checking via `never` type guard catches missing cases at compile time (regression #7 prevention; no `default:` swallow in the switch — the `default` case in the union is an explicit kind, not a fallthrough).
6. GIVEN FleetCard renders an epic WITHOUT a marker (most cards today), WHEN inspected, THEN existing default CTAs render AND no new visual elements appear AND existing FleetCard.attention.test.tsx passes unmodified.
7. GIVEN an epic with multiple `pipeline:*` labels (a6o drift) AND a marker for stage X matching the dashboard's currentStage=X, WHEN FleetCard renders, THEN the marker-driven CTA renders (NOT the multi-label-ambiguous default) — defends AC #5 of bead description.
8. GIVEN any marker-driven CTA button is clicked, WHEN dispatched, THEN `onPipelineAction` fires with an action name that exists in `agent-action-map.ts` AGENT_ACTION_MAP (no fabricated action names — the dispatcher would reject unknown actions).
9. GIVEN the integration test suite, WHEN `next build` runs (or test harness equivalent that exercises the full module graph), THEN no Edge Runtime build error occurs (no fs imports leak into the React tree per architect Watch-fors + ADR-002 + regression beads_web-8wh).
10. GIVEN tests run, THEN RTL tests pass against mocked `useEpicMarker` returning each `MarkerCtaIntent` kind AND mocked `onPipelineAction` (mocking pattern matches existing `FleetCard.attention.test.tsx`); integration test verifies the build succeeds end-to-end.
11. GIVEN tests cover ALL 5 precedence branches end-to-end (epic+marker fixture → FleetCard render → assertion on visible CTA), THEN regression coverage matches AC #6 of bead description.

## Depends on

- beads_web-374.3 (deriveMarkerCtaIntent + MarkerCtaIntent type — drives the switch).
- beads_web-374.4 (useEpicMarker — provides marker data to the component).

- `useEpicMarker` from 374.4.
- `deriveMarkerCtaIntent` + `MarkerCtaIntent` from 374.3.
- `onPipelineAction` callback + `PipelineActionPayload` shape (existing FleetBoard contract).
- AttentionBanner Tailwind classes (visual reference — copy the styling, do not import the component).
- Heroicons (existing dependency) for the badge icon.

## Coordinate (per bead-description NOTES)

- `beads_web-5nv` (P3) also edits FleetCard.tsx (populate pipeline-routes CTAs for all stages). 374.5 is the ONLY 374-bead that touches FleetCard.tsx — coordinate to avoid merge conflicts. Sequence so 5nv ships before or after 374.5 lands.

NOT folded into 374.5 (scope kept tight per architect's recommendation; niii.6's planner will decide whether to absorb or remain separate after 374 ships).

title: beads_web-374.4: useEpicMarker TanStack Query hook with stale-marker filtering
description:
## Outcome

Implement `useEpicMarker(epicId, stage, repoPath, qaRound?): { marker: MarkerData | null, isStale: boolean, isLoading: boolean }` as a TanStack Query hook in `src/hooks/useEpicMarker.ts`. Fetches the marker from 374.2's route. Implements stale-marker filtering per ADR-005 + AC #5 of bead description. Implements fail-degraded policy on fetch errors.

## Scope

- In: hook implementation; queryKey design; staleTime/refetchOnWindowFocus config; stale-marker filter; fail-degraded handling; tests.
- Out: any React component (374.5); any precedence interpretation (374.3 owns it); any direct fs imports (route is the only fs boundary per ADR-002 / Edge Runtime Constraints).

## Critical: queryKey MUST include repoPath

Per architect § Watch-fors for the builder + Risk 5 in o4lx investigation: two epics in DIFFERENT repos with the same epicId-prefix would otherwise share a cache entry. queryKey shape:

```ts
queryKey: ["marker", repoPath, markerId]
```

where `markerId = deriveMarkerId(epicId, stage, qaRound)` (374.1).

## Stale-marker filter (per ADR-005)

The hook computes `isStale = mapFleetStageToMarkerStage(currentStage) !== marker.stage` — with the exception that QA round markers (`<epicId>-qa-round-N`) count as fresh as long as the dashboard is on the QA stage. When isStale, the hook returns `{ marker: null, isStale: true }` — the component (374.5) sees `marker === null` → intent derives to `default` → fall-through to existing CTAs. This defends AC #5 of bead description (a6o label-hygiene drift) AND mirrors the filter shape `beads_web-85f` is expected to introduce.

## Fail-degraded policy (per architect § Failure modes at integration seams)

On fetch error, server 500, network failure, or `isError` from useQuery → return `{ marker: null, isStale: false, isLoading: false }`. Treat outage like missing marker. **The dashboard must remain operable when the marker route fails** — the operator can still dispatch via existing default CTAs.

## Cache config

- `staleTime: 30000` (30s — aligns with useIssues 15s polling; allows ~2 fleet-poll cycles before re-fetch).
- `refetchOnWindowFocus: true` (matches existing dashboard convention; useResearchReport precedent).

## Acceptance criteria

1. GIVEN valid epicId + stage + repoPath, WHEN hook mounts, THEN it fetches `/api/markers/[epicId]/[stage]?repoPath=<path>` AND returns `{ marker, isStale: false, isLoading: false }` after success.
2. GIVEN the queryKey shape, THEN it MUST include `repoPath` AND `markerId` (cross-repo cache safety per architect Watch-fors + o4lx Risk 5).
3. GIVEN a marker whose `stage` field doesn't match the dashboard's `currentStage` (per FleetStage→marker-stage mapping from 374.1), WHEN the hook returns, THEN `{ marker: null, isStale: true }` (stale-marker filter per ADR-005).
4. GIVEN an epic on QA stage with a `qa-round-3` marker AND dashboard `currentStage = qa`, WHEN the hook returns, THEN marker is fresh (NOT filtered as stale — QA round markers are fresh on the QA stage).
5. GIVEN the route returns 500 OR the fetch promise rejects OR returns malformed JSON, WHEN the hook returns, THEN `{ marker: null, isStale: false, isLoading: false }` (fail-degraded; FleetCard falls through to default CTAs unchanged).
6. GIVEN tests run, THEN they pass against mocked `fetch` returning the 374.2 route's response shape `{ marker: MarkerData | null }` (mocking pattern matches existing `useResearchReport` / `useAttentionItems` tests in `__tests__/components/`).
7. GIVEN tests cover the a6o-defence scenario (epic with multiple `pipeline:*` labels + a marker for stage X matching currentStage=X), WHEN the hook returns, THEN marker is returned (NOT filtered as stale) — defending against label-hygiene drift per AC #5 of bead description.
8. GIVEN tests run, THEN `staleTime: 30000` + `refetchOnWindowFocus: true` are configured AND the hook does not re-render on every parent render (TanStack Query memoizes via queryKey).

## Depends on

- beads_web-374.1 (deriveMarkerId — for markerId + mapFleetStageToMarkerStage).
- beads_web-374.2 (route exists at /api/markers/[epicId]/[stage]).

## Reuse (do NOT duplicate)

- `@tanstack/react-query` `useQuery` (existing dependency; pattern matches `useIssues`, `useResearchReport`, `useAttentionItems`).
- `deriveMarkerId`, `mapFleetStageToMarkerStage` from 374.1.
- `MarkerData` type from `marker-reader.ts` (type-only import OK — does NOT pull `fs` into the React tree because it is type-only).

## Standards / regressions

- code-principles.md § Next.js Edge Runtime Constraints — type-only imports of marker-reader.ts are OK; runtime imports are forbidden in the React tree.
- Regression #5 (Expensive Computation in Render Path) — TanStack Query memoizes; the stale check is O(1).

## Files

- src/hooks/useEpicMarker.ts
- __tests__/components/useEpicMarker.test.tsx

title: beads_web-374.3: deriveMarkerCtaIntent pure function + MarkerCtaIntent discriminated union
description:
## Outcome

Implement `deriveMarkerCtaIntent(marker: MarkerData | null, snapshot: EpicStateSnapshot, currentStage: FleetStage): MarkerCtaIntent` as a pure TypeScript function. Defines the `MarkerCtaIntent` discriminated union (4 cases: `marker-driven` | `needs-decision` | `failure` | `default`). REUSES `interpretMarkerForRouting` (do not duplicate the precedence rule).

## Scope

- In: `MarkerCtaIntent` type; `deriveMarkerCtaIntent` function; helpers (BLOCKER-line extraction, failure-stage→action mapping); tests.
- Out: any React rendering (374.5); any I/O; any precedence-rule re-implementation (REUSE the shipped `interpretMarkerForRouting` per ADR-001).

## ADR-001: REUSE precedence (do NOT duplicate)

The dashboard becomes a third caller of `interpretMarkerForRouting` (alongside `dispatchChainAction` and `marker-driven-routing.ts` reconciler rule). `deriveMarkerCtaIntent` calls it then post-processes the `RoutingDecision` plus marker fields into the four-case union. No second copy of the precedence rule, no second blocker-class table, no second action-name map.

This bead's correctness directly defends bead-description failure mode #1: "dashboard shows happy-path → operator clicks → wrong dispatch fires" happens specifically when the dashboard and orchestrator disagree on precedence. They cannot disagree if they call the same function.

## MarkerCtaIntent (per architect § Data Model)

```ts
type MarkerCtaIntent =
  | { kind: "marker-driven"; nextAgent: AgentType; action: string; reason: string; }
  | { kind: "needs-decision"; blockerMessage: string; coherenceAction: "run-coherence-agent"; reason: string; }
  | { kind: "failure"; stage: string; action: string; recommendation: string | null; reason: string; }
  | { kind: "default"; reason: string; };
```

## Acceptance criteria (cover ALL 5 precedence branches per AC #6 of bead description)

1. GIVEN a marker with `status: blocked` + `blocker_class: design-question` (maps to coherence per blocker-class table), WHEN deriveMarkerCtaIntent is called, THEN returns `{ kind: "needs-decision", coherenceAction: "run-coherence-agent", blockerMessage: <BLOCKER: text from whats_open> }`.
2. GIVEN a marker with explicit `next_agent: architect`, WHEN called, THEN returns `{ kind: "marker-driven", nextAgent: "architect", action: <getActionForAgent('architect')> }`.
3. GIVEN a marker with `status: blocked` + `blocker_class: <other-key>` (from blocker-class table), WHEN called, THEN returns `{ kind: "marker-driven" }` with the agent from the blocker-class table.
4. GIVEN a marker with `status: needs-decision` + `BLOCKER:` lines in whats_open, WHEN called, THEN returns `{ kind: "needs-decision" }` with the FIRST BLOCKER message extracted (per architect § Component Boundaries).
5. GIVEN a marker with `status: success` + no `next_agent`, WHEN called, THEN returns `{ kind: "default" }` (override=false; FleetCard renders existing CTAs unchanged — defends AC #4 of bead description).
6. GIVEN a marker with `status: failure`, WHEN called, THEN returns `{ kind: "failure", stage: marker.stage, action: <re-run action via getActionForAgent(marker.stage as AgentType)>, recommendation: marker.recommendation_for_next ?? null }`.
7. GIVEN `marker === null`, WHEN called, THEN returns `{ kind: "default" }`.
8. GIVEN the switch on `intent.kind` in tests, THEN exhaustive coverage is enforced via TypeScript `never` type guard (regression #7 prevention; no `default:` swallow).
9. GIVEN tests run, THEN they pass against in-memory `MarkerData` fixtures (no fs, no network) AND assert all 5 precedence branches from `interpretMarkerForRouting` are exercised through this function (per AC #6 of bead description) AND assert each `MarkerCtaIntent` kind is produced by at least one test case.

## Reuse (do NOT duplicate)

- `interpretMarkerForRouting(snapshot, marker): RoutingDecision` (`src/lib/marker-routing.ts`).
- `getActionForAgent(agentType): string` (`src/lib/agent-action-map.ts`).
- `MarkerData`, `AgentType`, `RoutingDecision`, `EpicStateSnapshot` types (existing).

## Standards / regressions

- agent-discipline.md § 2b Architecture Simplicity Gate (one new file ~80 lines, one new type).
- Regression #5 (Expensive Computation in Render Path) — pure function separated from JSX (per ADR-004); no React dependency.
- Regression #7 (Type Confusion on Enum Branching) — discriminated union with exhaustive switch; `never` type guard catches missing cases at compile.

## Files

- src/lib/derive-marker-cta-intent.ts
- __tests__/lib/derive-marker-cta-intent.test.ts

title: beads_web-374.2: Node-runtime API route /api/markers/[epicId]/[stage] (wraps readMarker)
description:
## Outcome

Add a Next.js Node-runtime API route at `src/app/api/markers/[epicId]/[stage]/route.ts` that wraps the existing `readMarker(repoPath, markerId)` (REUSE — `src/lib/marker-reader.ts`, shipped under o4lx.2). Returns parsed marker JSON or null over HTTP. This is the only server-side bridge the React tree may use to read marker files.

## Scope

- In: GET handler; input validation; `getAllRepoPaths()` whitelist enforcement; Node runtime + dynamic declarations; tests.
- Out: any modification to marker-reader.ts; any caching (TanStack Query handles it client-side per 374.4); WebSocket pushes; per-bead marker reads (out of scope per ADR-006).

## Critical: Edge Runtime trap

The route MUST declare:

```ts
export const runtime = "nodejs";
export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";
```

The first prevents the build from trying to bundle `fs/promises` for the edge runtime (regression beads_web-8wh — fs is unresolvable at edge build time, build fails). The second forces dynamic rendering since markers change.

NO file in the React tree (hooks, components) may import `marker-reader.ts` directly. The route is the boundary. The hook (374.4) talks to the route via fetch.

## Security boundary (architect § Security Architecture)

1. Validate `epicId` against `/^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+$/` (strict bead-ID character set; no `/`, no `..`, no leading `.`).
2. Validate `stage` against the closed set of FleetStage values (or marker-stage suffixes per 374.1 mapping).
3. Validate `repoPath` against the result of `getAllRepoPaths()` (existing whitelist used by `/api/research/[appName]`). Refuse any path NOT in the configured repo store.
4. Compose final path as `path.join(repoPath, ".beads", "markers", '<markerId>.json')` ONLY after the validations above.

## Acceptance criteria

1. GIVEN a valid epicId + stage URL params + whitelisted repoPath query string + an existing marker file, WHEN GET fires, THEN returns 200 with `{ marker: MarkerData }` (parsed marker JSON via readMarker).
2. GIVEN a valid request but the marker file is missing on disk, WHEN GET fires, THEN returns 200 with `{ marker: null }` (NOT 404 — null is a valid value per architect Interface Contracts table).
3. GIVEN a valid request but the marker file is malformed JSON, WHEN GET fires, THEN returns 200 with `{ marker: null }` (readMarker logs warning, returns null; route does not surface the error to the client).
4. GIVEN a `repoPath` query string NOT in `getAllRepoPaths()` whitelist, WHEN GET fires, THEN returns 400 (security boundary refuses non-whitelisted paths).
5. GIVEN an invalid `epicId` (contains `/`, `..`, or leading `.`), WHEN GET fires, THEN returns 400.
6. GIVEN an invalid `stage` (not in closed FleetStage set / marker-stage suffix set), WHEN GET fires, THEN returns 400.
7. GIVEN the route file is inspected, THEN it declares `export const runtime = "nodejs"` AND `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` (per ADR-002 + code-principles.md Edge Runtime Constraints).
8. GIVEN tests run, THEN they pass against mocked `fs.readFile` + mocked `getAllRepoPaths` returning a whitelist fixture (mocking pattern matches existing `/api/research/[appName]` test fixtures — `__tests__/api/agent.test.ts` or peer test).
9. GIVEN the existing build pipeline, WHEN `next build` runs, THEN no Edge Runtime build failure occurs.

## Reuse (do NOT duplicate)

- `readMarker(repoPath, markerId): Promise<MarkerData | null>` (`src/lib/marker-reader.ts`).
- `getAllRepoPaths(): Promise<string[]>` (`src/lib/repo-config.ts`).
- `MarkerData` interface (`src/lib/marker-reader.ts`).

## Standards / regressions

- code-principles.md § Next.js Edge Runtime Constraints (cites beads_web-8wh).
- agent-discipline.md § 2b Architecture Simplicity Gate (passed by architect; one new route handler, no new infra).
- Regression #13 (Silent Exception Swallowing) — readMarker returns null on parse error (logged); route does NOT swallow validation errors silently (returns 400).

## Files

- src/app/api/markers/[epicId]/[stage]/route.ts
- __tests__/api/markers-route.test.ts

title: beads_web-374.1: deriveMarkerId pure utility + FleetStage→marker-stage mapping
description:
## Outcome

Implement `deriveMarkerId(epicId, stage, qaRound?): string` and `mapFleetStageToMarkerStage(stage: FleetStage): string` as pure TypeScript utilities. Pure means: no React, no fs, no fetch. Testable as plain TS.

## Scope

- In: `deriveMarkerId`, `mapFleetStageToMarkerStage`, full FleetStage→marker-stage mapping table (per architect document § Data Model).
- Out: any I/O; any React hook; any consumer wiring (374.4 will consume).

## Mapping rules (architect doc § Data Model)

- `plan-review` → `planner` (the planner agent writes the marker; "plan-review" is a dashboard column name).
- `product-spec` → `product-manager`.
- All others identity (`architecture` → `architect`, `test-spec` → `test-spec`, `research` → `research`, `build-review` → `reviewer` or `build-review` per existing marker filenames — verify against `agent-action-map.ts` AGENT_ACTION_MAP).
- QA stage with `qaRound` defined → `<epicId>-qa-round-<N>` (per agent-launcher.ts:2017-2020 precedent).
- QA stage WITHOUT `qaRound` → `<epicId>-qa` (epic-scope QA marker).

## Acceptance criteria

1. GIVEN epicId + qa stage + qaRound=3, WHEN deriveMarkerId is called, THEN returns `<epicId>-qa-round-3`.
2. GIVEN epicId + plan-review stage (no qaRound), WHEN deriveMarkerId is called, THEN returns `<epicId>-planner`.
3. GIVEN epicId + product-spec stage, WHEN deriveMarkerId is called, THEN returns `<epicId>-product-manager`.
4. GIVEN epicId + architecture stage, WHEN deriveMarkerId is called, THEN returns `<epicId>-architect`.

title: [BUG] agent-launcher: stale markers from prior runs confuse detectAgentDone + routing
description:
**Source:** Pre-mortem memo `docs/research/pre-mortem-pipeline-readiness-2026-05-01.md` § 3 IF1 (lines 157-181).

## What breaks

When an epic has a marker from a prior agent run, and the operator re-dispatches the same agent type, `detectAgentDone` reads the OLD marker (>5s stale), sees `status=blocked`, and immediately marks the agent as done. `dispatchChainAction` then reads the same marker and routes incorrectly (coherence fallback if `blocker_class` is unset). Marker files are never deleted or archived. `detectAgentDone` checks marker age (>5s → stable) but not marker freshness relative to current agent session. A marker from a prior session is indistinguishable from a marker just written by the current session.

```typescript
  : beadId ?? null;
if (markerId) {
  const markerPath = path.join(repoPath, ".beads", "markers", `${markerId}.json`);
  try { await fs.unlink(markerPath); } catch { /* ignore ENOENT */ }
}
```

title: [BUG] marker-routing: status=blocked with no blocker_class falls through to default progression
description:
**Source:** Pre-mortem memo `docs/research/pre-mortem-pipeline-readiness-2026-05-01.md` § 3 IF2 (lines 183-217).

## What breaks

When an agent writes a marker with `status=blocked` but forgets to set `blocker_class`, the marker-routing logic returns `override=false` (no routing decision), which tells `dispatchChainAction` to fall through to pipeline-routes default progression.
```typescript
// Precedence 2.5: status=blocked with no blocker_class → coherence fallback
if (marker.status === "blocked") {
  return {
    override: true,
    nextAgent: "coherence",
```

title: Routing interpretation + blocker-class mapping
description:
**Source:** factory-core-o4lx (Phase 2 Wave 3 reopened — Intelligent marker-driven pipeline routing).

**Design source-of-truth:** factory-core/docs/research/o4lx-marker-driven-routing-investigation.md § 10 Bead 4 (architect memo, commit 2f085c3, 2026-05-01).

## Rationale

Core routing decision logic. Maps marker content (`status`, `next_agent`, `blocker_class`) to dispatch action. Reusable by inline branch (beads_web-<next-id>) and reconciler rule (beads_web-<later-id>).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **New file** `src/lib/marker-routing.ts` exports `interpretMarkerForRouting(marker: MarkerData, snapshot: EpicStateSnapshot): RoutingDecision`.

2. **Type `RoutingDecision`** includes `{ override: boolean; nextAgent?: string; action?: string; reason: string }`.

3. **Precedence implementation** (per memo § 6 Q4 precedence rule):
   - If `marker.next_agent` is set (non-null, non-empty) → `{ override: true, nextAgent: marker.next_agent, reason: "explicit next_agent field" }`.
   - Else if `marker.status === "blocked"` AND `marker.blocker_class` is set → map `blocker_class` to `nextAgent` via mapping table (AC 4), `override: true`.
   - Else if `marker.status === "needs-decision"` AND BLOCKER in `whats_open` → `{ override: true, nextAgent: "coherence", reason: "needs-decision with BLOCKER" }`.
   - Else if `marker.status === "success"` → `{ override: false, reason: "fallback to pipeline-routes" }`.
   - Else if `marker.status === "failure"` → `{ override: true, nextAgent: <same-agent>, reason: "re-dispatch on failure" }`.

4. **Blocker-class mapping table** (per memo § 4):
   - `design-question` → `architect`
   - `spec-ambiguity` → `product-manager`
   - `scope-conflict` → `coherence`
   - `test-fail` → `builder`
   - `file-conflict` → `planner`
   - `orchestrator-down` → `operator` (emit `review:needs-human` label)
   - Unknown blocker_class → `coherence` (fallback for unrecognized classes)

5. **Unit tests** (12 tests covering all precedence branches + blocker-class mappings + fallback cases):
   - Explicit `next_agent=architect` → `override=true, nextAgent="architect"`.
   - `status=blocked, blocker_class=design-question` → `override=true, nextAgent="architect"`.
   - `status=blocked, blocker_class=test-fail` → `override=true, nextAgent="builder"`.
   - `status=blocked, blocker_class=orchestrator-down` → `override=true, nextAgent="operator"`.
   - `status=blocked, blocker_class=unknown-value` → `override=true, nextAgent="coherence"` (fallback).
   - `status=needs-decision, whats_open=["BLOCKER: ..."]` → `override=true, nextAgent="coherence"`.
   - `status=success, next_agent` absent → `override=false` (fallback to pipeline-routes).
   - `status=failure` → `override=true, nextAgent=<same-agent>`.
   - Marker with both `next_agent` and `blocker_class` → `next_agent` wins (precedence).
   - Marker with `status=success` but `next_agent=planner` → `override=true, nextAgent="planner"` (explicit override beats status).
   - Edge: marker missing `status` field → treat as invalid, return `override=false` with `reason="invalid marker"`.
   - Edge: `whats_open` present but no BLOCKER prefix → treat as non-blocked, fall through to status-based logic.

**Empirical evidence (3p1e):** rounds 3–21 all PASS verdict, 0 bugs, `repeated-qa-round` rule never matched because of the early-exit. Operator hard-suppress was the only termination path.

**Expected behaviour:** Add a `roundsWithoutProgress >= K` predicate as a parallel branch. A round is "without progress" if its `openBugCount` equals the prior round's `openBugCount` AND verdict was PASS. Default K = 3. The new branch fires when K consecutive PASS-with-no-bug-delta rounds detected.

The existing predicate (round ≥ 5 AND `openBugCount > 0`) is preserved unchanged as the bugs-not-decreasing branch. The new branch handles the bugs-stuck-at-zero (and bugs-stuck-at-N>0-with-PASS) cases.

title: Add beads_web shutdown handler to reap Dolt processes on exit
description:
**Trigger:** Dolt-lifecycle leak surfaced during so74 Phase 2 work — beads_web exits without cleaning up Dolt sql-server processes that bd auto-spawned. ~43 orphaned Dolts consuming ~2.8GB RAM observed pre-cleanup.

**Source:** Diagnosis at `factory-core/docs/aspirational-pipeline/dolt-lifecycle-leak.md` (originally produced by `factory-core-8260.2`, since closed/compacted out of bd; the doc remains the authoritative reference).

## Behaviour to ship

1. Register `process.on('SIGTERM')` and `process.on('SIGINT')` in beads_web's lifecycle.
2. On signal, read `~/.beads-web.json`, enumerate repos, read each `.beads/dolt-server.pid`, send SIGTERM to each live Dolt PID.
3. Wait 5s for graceful shutdown; escalate to SIGKILL if needed.

## Bootstrap pattern (Q2 design decision, 2026-04-30)

Mirror `src/lib/reconciler-bootstrap.ts` — bootstrap via a route-handler self-fetch from `src/instrumentation.ts`, NOT direct registration in instrumentation.ts. Rationale: `instrumentation.ts` is webpack-compiled for both node and edge runtimes; static or dynamic imports of node-only modules (`child_process`, `fs` sync, `process.kill`) break the edge bundle. Route handlers are unambiguously Node-runtime and safe for those imports. The shutdown handler module (`src/lib/dolt-lifecycle.ts`) registers `process.on('SIGTERM'/'SIGINT')` once on first call to `ensureDoltLifecycleRegistered()` from a Node-runtime route handler, idempotent across hot-reloads.

Suggested route: `/api/fleet/dolt-lifecycle/init` (or co-locate with reconciler bootstrap if appropriate — builder/architect call). The route is self-fetched from instrumentation.ts after a delay, same pattern as `factory-core-6wrk.1` self-fetch to `/api/fleet/reconciler/status`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. On beads_web SIGTERM/SIGINT, all Dolt sql-server processes referenced by `~/.beads-web.json` registry repos are killed via SIGTERM (5s grace, then SIGKILL). Per Q1c (2026-04-30), F3 alive-set protection is OUT OF SCOPE here — see `beads_web-c28` for that follow-up.
2. On clean beads_web restart (next dev hot-reload), no orphaned Dolt processes remain from the prior session.
3. Handler reads repos from `~/.beads-web.json` (use existing `src/lib/repo-config.ts:getRepos()` or `getAllRepoPaths()`) and checks `.beads/dolt-server.pid` per repo.
4. Unit test at `__tests__/lib/dolt-lifecycle.test.ts`: mock process signals and `process.kill`, verify cleanup function is invoked with correct PIDs read from registry repos' `.beads/dolt-server.pid` files.
5. Bootstrap pattern: `dolt-lifecycle.ts` module exports an idempotent `ensureDoltLifecycleRegistered()` that registers signal handlers once per process; called from a Node-runtime route handler self-fetched by `instrumentation.ts` (mirrors `reconciler-bootstrap.ts` pattern).

## Files (manifest)

- beads_web/src/lib/dolt-lifecycle.ts (NEW)
- beads_web/src/instrumentation.ts (modify — add self-fetch trigger for the new bootstrap route)
- beads_web/src/app/api/fleet/dolt-lifecycle/init/route.ts (NEW — bootstrap route, mirrors reconciler-status pattern)
- beads_web/__tests__/lib/dolt-lifecycle.test.ts (NEW)

## Dependencies

- Diagnosis doc: `factory-core/docs/aspirational-pipeline/dolt-lifecycle-leak.md` (authoritative root-cause reference).
- Pattern reference: `beads_web/src/lib/reconciler-bootstrap.ts` (route-handler self-fetch model).

## Migration note

Migrated from `factory-core-8260.5` (no longer in bd; closed/compacted) per Wave 2 routing rule — target files are in beads_web/src/, so the bead lives in beads_web's bd.

Cross-repo epic linkage is via `epic:factory-core-so74` label, not via bd `--parent`. Note that so74 itself auto-closed 2026-04-30 when so74.1 closed; this bead is now an orphaned Phase 2 follow-up tracked in factory-core's `state-of-the-shipyard.md` under "Phase 2 follow-ups (open hygiene)".

## Operator decisions baked in (2026-04-30)

- **Q1c:** F3 (cleanup-preserves-alive-set rule) split out as `beads_web-c28` rather than folded in. 6pf ships the literal "kill every registry Dolt" procedure; alive-set protection is the c28 follow-up.
- **Q2b:** Bootstrap via route-handler self-fetch (mirroring `reconciler-bootstrap.ts`), not direct registration in `instrumentation.ts` — see "Bootstrap pattern" section above.

Kill sequence: SIGTERM -> 5s grace -> SIGKILL. PID verification via ps guards against stale/recycled PIDs. F3 alive-set OUT OF SCOPE per Q1c, deferred to beads_web-c28. Commit 5b97e14.

title: QA: Auto-chain actions omit currentLabels, defaulting ship type to ios-app for all chained pipeline stages
notes:
**What's wrong:** When the pipeline auto-chains between stages (e.g., development -> QA, research -> planning, planning -> build, qa -> qa-fix-and-retest, qa-fixes -> QA), the fetch calls in src/lib/agent-launcher.ts (lines 199, 221, 243, 286, 306) do not pass currentLabels in the request body. This causes src/app/api/fleet/action/route.ts:136 to produce an empty labels array, and line 139 to default shipType to 'ios-app' regardless of the epic's actual ship type.

**Root cause:** All five handleChainAction fetch calls in agent-launcher.ts only pass action, epicId, and epicTitle -- never currentLabels. The shipType extraction at route.ts:138-139 depends on finding a 'ship-type:*' label in currentLabels.

**Impact:** When a non-iOS product (e.g., web-app, wordpress-plugin, python-tool) auto-chains from development to QA, the QA agent selection at route.ts:515-518 evaluates shipType='ios-app', causing 'ios'.replace('-app','')='ios' to match the platformQA array. This loads platforms/ios/qa agent instead of the generic qa agent. The QA prompt also tells the agent the wrong ship type.

**Expected behavior:** Auto-chained actions should resolve the epic's actual ship type. Either pass currentLabels in the chain fetch call (requires reading labels from the epic), or persist the ship type in the AgentSession so it can be forwarded.

**Suggested fix:** Add the epic's labels to the chain action fetch body. The simplest approach: store labels on the AgentSession object (add a labels field to the session at launch time, persist it), then forward them in handleChainAction fetch calls as currentLabels.

title: Marker-aware CTAs in FleetCard — bead-card buttons reflect marker.next_agent + interpretMarkerForRouting precedence (not just labels)
description:
## Empirical evidence (2026-05-01)

`src/components/fleet/FleetCard.tsx` (1192 lines) is the dashboard's bead-card component. Its CTA-rendering logic reads ONLY label-derived state and is completely disjoint from the reconciler's marker-routing logic.

Empirical confirmation:
- `grep -nE "marker|next_agent|pipeline-routes|interpretMarker" src/components/fleet/FleetCard.tsx` → **zero references**.
- FleetCard imports: labels via `isAgentRunning, getPhaseHistory, getWaveInfo, classifyPlanReviewSubState, deriveCurrentRound, FLEET_STAGE_CONFIG`. CTAs are hardcoded per-stage in JSX blocks (e.g., `Start Research` button at line 489, `Skip to Plan` at 497, `review-wave` at 533).
- Reconciler precedence at `src/lib/marker-routing.ts:104-202` (`interpretMarkerForRouting`):
  1. Explicit `next_agent` field → dispatch that agent
  2. status=blocked + blocker_class → blocker-class table
  3. status=needs-decision + BLOCKER → coherence
  4. status=success → fallback to pipeline-routes
  5. status=failure → re-dispatch same agent

The dashboard does not mirror this precedence. Result: bead-card CTAs may show the happy-path next-stage button while the marker actually says the bead needs operator/coherence intervention.

## Concrete failure modes

1. **Marker says `next_agent: coherence` (blocker_class=design-question)** → dashboard shows happy-path "Send for development" → operator clicks → wrong dispatch fires.
2. **Marker says `next_agent: operator` (unresolved tension)** → dashboard shows next-stage CTA → operator never sees the "needs decision" state.
3. **Marker says `status: needs-decision` with `BLOCKER:` in `whats_open`** → dashboard shows nothing distinguishing → silent escalation; operator must inspect markers manually.
4. **Marker says `status: failure`** → dashboard may show "advance" button → operator unknowingly skips a failure that should re-dispatch the same agent.
5. **Multiple `pipeline:*` labels (per `beads_web-a6o` label-hygiene drift)** → CTAs render for whichever pipeline label JSX matches first → wrong stage's CTAs.

## Scope

Make FleetCard's CTA rendering marker-aware. New data flow:

1. **New hook: `useEpicMarker(epicId, currentStage)`** — reads the latest marker for the epic at the current stage path: `<repoPath>/.beads/markers/<epicId>-<stage>.json` (epic-scope) or `<repoPath>/.beads/markers/<beadId>.json` (per-bead). Returns parsed `MarkerData | null`.
2. **Apply `interpretMarkerForRouting` at render time** — call the existing function (already exported per the audit's verification at IF6) with the epic's snapshot. Get the routing decision.
3. **CTA rendering logic** — branch on the routing decision:
   - `override=true, nextAgent=X` → show CTA for action mapped to agent X (use `getActionForAgent` from `agent-action-map.ts`).
   - `override=false` (status=success, no next_agent) → fall back to existing pipeline-routes CTAs (same as today).
   - status=needs-decision with BLOCKER → render distinct visual state ("Needs decision — review marker context") with coherence dispatch button.
   - status=failure → render "Re-run <stage>" button (calls same stage's resume action).

## Visual treatment

- **Marker-driven CTA** (override=true): primary button label reflects the next agent (e.g., "Run coherence", "Notify operator", "Run product manager"). Visual badge: small marker icon next to button to indicate "marker-suggested action".
- **Pipeline-routes default CTA** (override=false): unchanged from today — happy-path next-stage button.
- **Needs-decision state**: yellow/amber styling matching existing `attention-banner` patterns. Surface the `whats_open` BLOCKER message inline.
- **Failure state**: orange/red styling. Surface `recommendation_for_next` text from marker.

## Acceptance criteria

GIVEN an epic with a marker file containing `next_agent: <agent>` AND status=success, WHEN FleetCard renders the bead card, THEN the primary CTA reflects `getActionForAgent(<agent>)` (not the pipeline-routes default).

GIVEN an epic with a marker containing `status: needs-decision` AND `BLOCKER:` in `whats_open`, WHEN FleetCard renders, THEN a distinct "Needs decision" visual state is shown AND the BLOCKER message is surfaced inline AND a coherence dispatch button is offered.

GIVEN an epic with a marker containing `status: failure`, WHEN FleetCard renders, THEN the primary CTA is "Re-run <stage>" (same-stage resume action) AND `recommendation_for_next` is surfaced inline.

GIVEN an epic with no marker file OR a marker with no routing intent (status=success + no next_agent), WHEN FleetCard renders, THEN existing pipeline-routes default CTAs render unchanged (current behaviour preserved).

GIVEN an epic with marker AND multiple `pipeline:*` labels (label drift per a6o), WHEN FleetCard renders, THEN the marker's stage takes precedence over the labels for CTA selection (defensive against label-hygiene bugs).

GIVEN the regression test suite, WHEN run after this change, THEN no existing tests fail AND new tests cover all 5 precedence branches above.

## Cross-references / interactions

- **`beads_web-5nv`** (P3, populate pipeline-routes CTAs for all stages) — this bead is the marker-aware overlay; 5nv is the static-config sweep. They both edit FleetCard.tsx — coordinate to avoid merge conflicts.
- **`beads_web-a6o`** (P3, pipeline label hygiene drift) — same label-state input. AC #5 above defends against a6o regressions.
- **`beads_web-85f`** (P2, reconciler stale-marker re-dispatch) — same marker-staleness concern. Stale-marker filtering in `useEpicMarker` should mirror whatever filter 85f introduces (skip markers from stages older than current).
- **`beads_web-07p`** (P3, stuck-in-stage silent dispatch observability) — orthogonal but related: when CTA dispatch fails, surface that on the bead card too.
- **`marker-routing.ts:104-202`** (`interpretMarkerForRouting`) — canonical precedence logic to mirror.
- **`agent-action-map.ts`** (extracted by `qfd`) — `getActionForAgent` mapping; reuse here.

## Why P2

- Operator dispatches happen through bead cards. Wrong CTAs → wrong dispatches → wasted agent runs + token budget.
- Failure states currently invisible to operator without manual marker inspection — defeats the autonomous-pipeline-with-operator-oversight design.
- Compound risk with a6o and 85f — label drift + stale marker re-dispatch + label-driven CTAs all point at the same UI being unreliable.
- Pipeline can still progress through curl as workaround, but the workaround is exactly what 5nv was filed to eliminate.

## Effort estimate

~4-6 hours: hook design + render-time precedence wiring + visual states for needs-decision/failure + tests across 5 precedence branches + manual verification against niii's current `pipeline:build-review` state.

## Out of scope

- Marker schema changes (covered by `factory-core-sy3d`/`sy3d.1`/`sy3d.2`).
- Reconciler-side changes (mirror existing logic, don't re-implement).
- Per-bead marker reads for non-epic beads (beads inherit epic state for now; per-bead marker UI is a follow-on).

`factory-core-niii.6` is a P3 follow-on filed 2026-05-01 to add a "Close Epic" button to the dashboard that calls `tools/generic/epic-close-gate.sh`. Per niii's architect memo (`docs/architecture/niii-auto-close-cascade-fix.md`), this is currently a CLI-only feature; niii.6 ports it to the dashboard UI.

niii.6's button is one specific CTA on bead cards. It overlaps directly with 374's scope (marker-aware CTA framework on FleetCard). When 374's planner runs:

- Alternatively, sequence niii.6 to ship AFTER 374.5 so niii.6 reuses 374.5's `useEpicMarker` hook + the marker-aware rendering precedence rather than adding a parallel data flow.

title: Reconciler re-dispatches from stale per-stage markers — IF1 fix incomplete (markers persist; fs-walk fallback re-fires completed stages)
description:
## Empirical evidence (2026-05-01)

The factory-core-niii epic's reconciler activity log shows `marker-driven-routing` firing for already-completed stages while a downstream agent is actively running:

| Time | Rule | Stage matched | Status when fired |
|------|------|---------------|-------------------|
| 21:46:42Z | marker-driven-routing | niii::architect | architect already exited 21:36:55Z; planner already running |
| 22:47:58Z | marker-driven-routing | niii::architect | architect long-completed; niii.1 builder running |
| 23:03:16Z | marker-driven-routing | niii::planner | planner already exited 21:57:09Z; niii.1 builder running |

The factory-core-niii architect and planner markers remain on disk with `next_agent` set:
- `.beads/markers/factory-core-niii-architect.json` (next_agent: planner)
- `.beads/markers/factory-core-niii-planner.json` (next_agent: test-spec)

The fs-walk fallback in `marker-driven-routing.ts:191-260` walks `.beads/markers/` in registered repos when event-based discovery returns zero matches. Its only "stale" guard is checking `bead.status === "open"`. Since `factory-core-niii` (the epic) IS open, fs-walk dispatches based on the architect/planner stage markers — even though those agents have long completed and a downstream stage is running.

Idempotency keys for the re-fires:
- `marker-driven-routing::factory-core-niii::architect` — fired at 21:46:42 AND 22:47:58 (same key, different windows: ~1h apart)
- `marker-driven-routing::factory-core-niii::planner` — fired at 23:03:16 (no prior key in observed window)

So the idempotency check either has a TTL that allows refires after ~1h, or the prior fire's record fell out of the lookback window.

## Why this matters (overlap with IF1 from pre-mortem)

Pre-mortem `docs/research/pre-mortem-pipeline-readiness-2026-05-01.md` § IF1 (lines 193-218) flagged:

> Stale markers from old runs confuse routing — orphan markers cause re-dispatch confusion.

The pipeline-readiness audit (`docs/audit/pipeline-readiness-ac-audit-2026-05-01.md` line 28) recorded IF1 as RESOLVED via `beads_web-2gc`:

> IF1 (stale markers): Resolved by 2gc | RESOLVED | agent-launcher.ts:3206-3228: stale marker deleted before tmux spawn. 6 tests pass.

The 2gc fix deletes the SAME stage's prior marker right before spawning a new agent of that stage (e.g., when re-dispatching test-spec, delete the prior test-spec marker). It does NOT delete markers from PRIOR stages of the same epic. The architect's marker persists through the planner run; the planner's marker persists through test-spec; etc. As long as those markers stay on disk with `next_agent` set, the fs-walk fallback can match them.

So IF1 is partially resolved (intra-stage stale markers handled) but inter-stage stale-marker re-dispatch is unaddressed.

## Where the bug lives

`src/lib/reconciler-rules/marker-driven-routing.ts`:
- Lines 191-260: fs-walk fallback. The `bead.status === "open"` filter is insufficient for epic-scope markers because the epic stays OPEN through every stage.
- Need an additional filter: skip markers where the marker's STAGE is older than the bead's CURRENT STAGE (derived from `pipeline:*` label).

`src/lib/agent-launcher.ts:3206-3228`:
- Current stale-marker cleanup is per-stage (delete the SAME stage's marker before spawning that stage). Could extend to delete ALL prior-stage markers when advancing.

`src/lib/pipeline-routes.ts` (or similar):
- The reconciler should know the canonical stage progression so it can identify "marker is for a stage older than current" and skip.

## Fix shape

Two complementary changes:

1. **fs-walk filter: skip markers from stages older than current.** Read the epic's `pipeline:*` label; compare to the marker's `stage` field. If marker.stage precedes pipeline-stage in the canonical progression, skip the match. Implement in `marker-driven-routing.ts:matches()` after the bead-status check.

2. **Stage-advance cleanup: delete prior-stage markers when label advances.** When the action route handler updates `pipeline:X → pipeline:Y`, delete `.beads/markers/<epicId>-<X>.json`. Implement in `pipeline-labels.ts:removeAllPipelineLabels` or wherever the label-advance happens.

Either alone reduces the re-fire surface; together they belt-and-braces eliminate the class.

## Acceptance criteria

GIVEN an epic at pipeline:development with prior-stage markers on disk (architect, planner, test-spec), WHEN the reconciler ticks AND fs-walk fallback runs, THEN markers for completed stages (anything before development in the canonical progression) are skipped AND only the current-stage marker (or newer) can match.

GIVEN an epic advances from pipeline:X to pipeline:Y, WHEN the label transition occurs (via action route), THEN `.beads/markers/<epicId>-<X>.json` is deleted (or moved to an archive subdir for forensic purposes).

GIVEN the niii reproduction scenario (architect+planner markers on disk while builder runs), WHEN the reconciler ticks, THEN `marker-driven-routing` does NOT fire for `architect` or `planner` stages.

GIVEN the regression test for IF1 (replays stale markers), WHEN run after this fix, THEN no spurious re-dispatches occur for completed stages.

## Why P2

- Active re-dispatches consume reconciler capacity (every tick, fs-walk re-walks the same stale markers).
- Re-dispatches MAY launch duplicate agents if `agent-launcher.isAgentActive` doesn't catch them in time. We can't currently verify if they actually launched (see `beads_web-07p` for the observability gap).
- Confuses operator diagnosis: reading recentActions, you see "marker-driven-routing fired for architect" while an architect is supposedly long-completed. Looks like a regression to a fresh observer.
- Probably explains some of the label drift in `beads_web-a6o` (re-dispatch of architect would set pipeline:architecture, then planner sets pipeline:plan-review, etc., explaining why pipeline:test-spec reappeared without a true test-spec dispatch).

## Cross-reference

- Pre-mortem IF1: `docs/research/pre-mortem-pipeline-readiness-2026-05-01.md:193-218`
- Audit (claimed RESOLVED): `docs/audit/pipeline-readiness-ac-audit-2026-05-01.md` line 28
- Original IF1 fix (2gc): `agent-launcher.ts:3206-3228`
- Related: `beads_web-07p` (silent dispatch failure observability — needed to know if these fs-walk re-fires actually launched agents)
- Related: `beads_web-a6o` (label hygiene drift — partially explained by re-dispatches)

title: start-wave dispatches only one builder per call — Wave parallelism lost (planner said niii.1+niii.2 parallel; only niii.1 launched)
description:
## Empirical evidence (2026-05-01)

Operator dispatched `POST /api/fleet/action {action: "start-wave", waveNumber: 1}` for `factory-core-niii`. The plan (per planner output) explicitly said:

> Beads 1+2 can run in parallel (Wave 1); bead 3 depends on bead 1 (Wave 2); bead 4 is independent doc update (Wave 1 or 2).

Neither niii.1 nor niii.2 has a blocking dependency on the other; no shared file conflict per the planner's design.

**What happened:**
1. start-wave returned `success: true` and launched ONE tmux session: `shipyard-factory-core-niii-development-wave1-factory-core-niii-1`.
2. niii.1 builder ran ~19 minutes, exited successfully, wrote a per-bead marker with `next_agent: test-spec`, and was auto-closed by bd.
3. **90 seconds after niii.1 closed, niii.2 was still status=OPEN with no tmux session.** No auto-dispatch.

So `start-wave` either:
- (a) Dispatches the FIRST eligible bead in the wave only, leaving siblings to be triggered by some other mechanism (which didn't trigger here either), OR
- (b) Has a single-process serialisation guard that prevents concurrent builders despite the plan saying parallel, OR
- (c) Treats wave-1 as "the next available bead" rather than "all beads tagged wave:1".

## Where the bug likely lives

`src/app/api/fleet/action/route.ts` — `start-wave` action handler. Inspect for:
- `groupBeadsByFileConflict` — may be returning a single bead for the whole wave even when no conflicts exist.
- `listOpenWaveBeads` — verify it returns all wave-1 beads, not just one.
- `launchAgent` call site — is it inside a loop over wave beads, or a single call?

Also relevant: `src/lib/agent-launcher.ts` — `launchAgent` may have a "one-active-builder-per-epic" guard that's too aggressive.

## Acceptance criteria

GIVEN an epic with N beads tagged for the same wave (e.g., wave:1) AND no blocking dependencies between them AND no shared-file conflicts, WHEN `start-wave` is invoked, THEN N tmux sessions are launched concurrently AND N builder agents run in parallel.

GIVEN an epic where Wave 1 has 2 parallel beads (per the niii test case: niii.1 + niii.2), WHEN start-wave fires, THEN both `shipyard-...niii-1` AND `shipyard-...niii-2` tmux sessions exist concurrently.

GIVEN an epic where wave beads have file conflicts detected by `groupBeadsByFileConflict`, WHEN start-wave fires, THEN beads in different conflict groups dispatch in parallel AND beads within a conflict group dispatch sequentially (existing intended behaviour preserved).

GIVEN the niii epic specifically (Wave 1: niii.1 + niii.2 with no conflicts), WHEN start-wave fires, THEN the regression test verifies both builders launch.

## Why P2

Functional pipeline still progresses, just at half speed. For waves with N parallel beads, dispatch latency multiplies by N (each bead waits for the prior to complete). Tolerable but eliminates the throughput benefit of wave-based parallelism.

## Cross-reference

- niii planner marker: `.beads/markers/factory-core-niii-planner.json` (recommendation_for_next field).
- niii.1 builder marker: `.beads/markers/factory-core-niii.1.json` (closed at ~23:09Z).
- niii.2 status: still OPEN at 23:11Z (90s after niii.1 closed) per `bd show factory-core-niii.2`.
notes:
**2026-05-01 23:25Z — empirical reframing: bug is a planner LABEL ASSIGNMENT issue, not a dispatcher behaviour issue.**

When the wave1 coordinator builder exited at 23:23:35Z, snapshot of niii children's wave labels:

| Bead | wave: label | Planner's prose intent |
|------|-------------|------------------------|
| niii.1 | wave:1 | wave:1 ✓ |
| niii.2 | **wave:2** | **wave:1 (parallel with niii.1)** ❌ |
| niii.3 | wave:2 | wave:2 ✓ |
| niii.4 | wave:2 | wave:1 OR wave:2 (independent) — ambiguous |
| niii.5/.6/.7 | (no label) | follow-ons, no wave (correct) |

The planner's `recommendation_for_next` field said *"Beads 1+2 can run in parallel (Wave 1); bead 3 depends on bead 1 (Wave 2); bead 4 is independent doc update (Wave 1 or 2)"* but the actual `wave:` labels assigned have **niii.2 in wave:2, not wave:1**. The dispatch system worked correctly given the labels — wave1 coordinator found niii.1 already closed → no remaining wave:1 work → exited cleanly. niii.2 was correctly NOT picked up because it's labeled wave:2.

So the bug surface SHIFTS:
- **NOT a parallelism dispatch bug.** start-wave's wave-coordinator correctly works wave:1 beads.
- **IS a planner label assignment bug.** The planner's prose intent didn't match the labels it set. Either the planner agent's logic for translating its plan into wave labels is broken, OR the planner deliberately set wave:2 for niii.2 (in which case the prose was wrong).

This reframes the fix surface from `src/app/api/fleet/action/route.ts` (start-wave handler) to:
- `.claude/agents/planner.md` — the planner agent's instructions for wave-label assignment.
- Possibly a label-validation step that runs after planner exit to verify wave labels match the plan's parallelism intent.

The first observation in this bead (first-call dispatches one bead, subsequent dispatches wave coordinator) is a SEPARATE behavior of start-wave that's NOT necessarily a bug — the first-call per-bead launch may be intentional (start a specific bead with `targetBeadId`); the wave-coordinator mode runs on subsequent calls. That asymmetry should be documented but isn't necessarily wrong.

**Updated AC focus:** GIVEN a planner produces a plan with N parallel-eligible beads in Wave K, WHEN the planner sets `wave:` labels on those beads, THEN all N beads receive `wave:K` (not wave:K+1). Verify by reading the plan file's parallelism statements and cross-checking against actual `wave:` labels at planner-exit.

**Priority unchanged at P2** — still functionally important (Wave parallelism delivers N× throughput when fixed) but lower-urgency since pipeline still progresses sequentially.

title: xfc filesystem-walk fallback for orphaned markers
description:
**Operator decision (2026-05-01, lmxb routing analysis):** Extend xfc reconciler rule (or file as new sibling rule) to ALSO walk `.beads/markers/*.json` periodically, catching orphaned markers that have no corresponding `agent-exited` event (e.g. markers written before o4lx shipped, markers where the event log was rotated/lost).

## Source

- `factory-core/docs/research/o4lx-marker-driven-routing-investigation.md` § 5 — architect originally recommended "periodic walk of recently-touched markers" (filesystem-based).
- `beads_web-xfc` (commit `840e4c1`) — shipped as event-based ("matches on `agent-exited` events") instead. The shift from filesystem-walk → event-based happened between architect memo and bead AC, undetected at bake time.
- `factory-core/docs/research/lmxb-routing-gap-analysis-2026-05-01.md` (this session) — documented the gap; lmxb canary cannot route despite correct marker because the trigger event already passed.

## Why this matters

Three classes of orphaned-marker scenarios that current xfc misses:
1. Markers written BEFORE o4lx routing existed (lmxb canary).
2. Markers where the event log was rotated, daemon restarted, etc., losing the corresponding `agent-exited` event.
3. Markers written by external tools / scripts that don't go through `agent-launcher.ts` and therefore don't emit `agent-exited` events.

## Acceptance criteria (sketch)

1. xfc rule (or new sibling rule, architect-decided) includes a filesystem-walk path: enumerate `.beads/markers/*.json` for each registered repo, identify markers whose bead is OPEN AND has `next_agent`/`blocker_class` set AND no recent dispatch event (idempotency fingerprint check).
2. For each candidate orphaned marker: invoke `interpretMarkerForRouting(marker)` (gc2's pure function) and dispatch the named agent if `override=true`.
3. Idempotency: don't double-dispatch. Use existing `dispatch-fingerprint.ts` or marker-action-fingerprint check.
4. Throttle: filesystem walk is more expensive than event-based matching; throttle to ~5 min cadence (or whatever architect recommends).
5. Unit tests: orphaned marker (no event) + open bead + has routing → dispatch fires; orphaned marker + closed bead → skip; orphaned marker + recent dispatch event → skip (idempotency).
6. Integration test: drop a synthetic orphaned marker for a test bead → xfc fires → correct agent dispatched within tick interval.
7. Single beads_web commit. NEW MARKER ORDERING applies.

## Phase 0 questions (likely needs architect)

**Q1 (extend xfc vs new rule):** add filesystem-walk path to existing xfc, OR file a new `marker-orphan-recovery.ts` rule that's purely filesystem-based? Architect recommendation needed; tradeoff is single-rule complexity vs duplication-of-logic.

**Q2 (idempotency mechanism):** does dispatch-fingerprint.ts cover this case, or does it need extension to fingerprint marker-driven dispatches (vs event-driven)?

**Q3 (throttle interval):** architect recommendation. Filesystem walk over 40 repos × N markers each could be expensive if every reconciler tick. Likely 5-min cadence is sufficient.

**Q4 (registered-repo scope):** walk all repos in `~/.beads-web.json`, or only repos referenced in recent events? Default lean: all registered repos (matches operator's expectation that any repo's markers are honored).

## Effort estimate

~2 hours (architect Q1-Q4 ~30 min + extend xfc or new rule ~1 hour + tests ~30 min).

## Cross-repo note

Bead filed in beads_web bd (code lives there). Unblocks lmxb-class scenarios where marker exists but dispatch trigger has already passed.

title: Pipeline label hygiene drift — stop-agent + start-wave leaves stale pipeline:test-spec, never sets pipeline:development, agent:running stuck without tmux
description:
## Empirical evidence (2026-05-01)

During factory-core-niii test-spec recovery:

1. **stop-agent** called → response `success: true, stopped: true`. Tmux session terminated. Labels AFTER stop-agent: `pipeline:plan-review, pipeline:test-spec, plan:pending, ship-type:internal` — TWO pipeline labels (one of them stale).
2. **Manual cleanup:** operator removed both pipeline labels via `bd update --remove-label`. Labels: `plan:pending, ship-type:internal`.
3. **start-wave** with waveNumber=1 → response `success: true`. Builder tmux session created. Labels AFTER start-wave: `plan:pending, ship-type:internal` — **`pipeline:development` was NEVER set.**
4. niii.1 builder ran ~19 min, exited successfully, was auto-closed. Labels DURING / AFTER builder run: `agent:running, pipeline:test-spec, plan:pending, ship-type:internal` — **`pipeline:test-spec` reappeared from somewhere AND `agent:running` got stuck on with no tmux session present.**

Three distinct label-hygiene issues:

**Issue A: stop-agent doesn't clean up pipeline labels properly.** After stop-agent, the bead had TWO pipeline labels simultaneously (plan-review AND test-spec). One should have been removed.

**Issue B: start-wave does not set `pipeline:development`.** The bead's canonical pipeline label remained at whatever was set before. The launcher knows the stage (encoded in tmux session name `...development-wave1...`) but doesn't update the bd label.

**Issue C: `agent:running` label gets stuck without a corresponding tmux session.** liveness-check is supposed to handle this but doesn't always fire in time. May overlap with reconciler re-dispatches resetting the label without tmux actually launching.

## Where the bug likely lives

`src/app/api/fleet/action/route.ts`:
- `stop-agent` handler — should remove the pipeline label of the stopped agent's stage (or revert to the prior stage's label).
- `start-wave` handler — should call `addLabelsToEpic('pipeline:development')` AND `removeLabelsFromEpic` for prior pipeline labels.

`src/lib/pipeline-labels.ts`:
- Verify `removeAllPipelineLabels` is called from start-wave and stop-agent paths.

`src/lib/reconciler-rules/liveness-check.ts`:
- Throttle / firing schedule — may need tightening if `agent:running` regularly drifts vs tmux state.

## Acceptance criteria

GIVEN an epic with `pipeline:X, agent:running` AND a running tmux session, WHEN stop-agent is invoked, THEN tmux session terminates AND `agent:running` is removed AND `pipeline:X` either remains (if X is still the stage) or is replaced with the prior stage's label (single pipeline label invariant).

GIVEN an epic with `pipeline:X` (any X) AND no agent running, WHEN start-wave is invoked AND a builder launches, THEN labels become `pipeline:development, agent:running, ship-type:Y, plan:pending` AND any prior `pipeline:*` labels are removed.

GIVEN a tmux session terminates (agent exits naturally), WHEN the next reconciler tick runs, THEN `agent:running` is cleared within 60 seconds AND the pipeline label advances per the marker's `next_agent` (or the pipeline-routes default if `next_agent` is missing).

GIVEN an epic in any pipeline stage, WHEN `bd label list <epic>` is run, THEN at most ONE `pipeline:*` label is present (single-pipeline invariant).

## Why P3

Cosmetic — does not block dispatch. Builders still launch via tmux session names (which encode stage). But:
- Dashboard groupings by `pipeline:*` label are wrong.
- Reconciler rules that key off `currentStage` (derived from pipeline label) may misroute.
- Operator confusion when manually inspecting.

Could escalate to P2 if reconciler routing demonstrably misfires due to label drift.

## Cross-reference

- Related bead: `factory-core-sy3d` (agent marker quality umbrella).
- Related bead: `beads_web-07p` (stuck-in-stage silent dispatch failure).
- Related bead (filed in same observation session): wave parallelism bug.

title: stuck-in-stage rule's dispatch silently fails to launch agent — fire recorded but no tmux session created
description:
## Empirical evidence (2026-05-01)

During the factory-core-niii test-spec stuck-in-stage observation window, the rule fired exactly when expected (15 min after the test-spec marker write at 22:27:42Z) but the dispatch did NOT produce a running agent.

**Timeline:**
- 22:25:01.326Z — first stuck-in-stage fire on niii (window 1777673700000) — DID launch test-spec successfully (tmux session created, agent ran, marker written 22:27:42Z)
- 22:27:42Z — test-spec marker written with `status=success` and `next_agent: <MISSING>` (orphan marker — see `factory-core-sy3d.1`)
- 22:34:43Z — `agent:running` label cleared (mechanism unidentified — neither liveness-check nor stuck-in-stage was the actor per recentActions)
- 22:43:37.665Z — second stuck-in-stage fire on niii (window 1777674600000)
- 22:44:52Z — direct verification: `tmux ls | grep niii` returns nothing; test-spec marker mtime unchanged; bd labels show no agent:running. **The 22:43:37 dispatch produced no running agent.**
- 22:45:25.640Z — manual `POST /api/fleet/action` with identical payload (action=run-test-spec, same epicId, same currentLabels) returned `success: true` and DID launch the tmux session `shipyard-factory-core-niii-test-spec`.

So the rule's act() at 22:43:37 made the fetch (recorded in recentActions), but somewhere between fetch and tmux-spawn the launch was silently dropped. My identical manual POST 108 seconds later succeeded.

## Where the bug likely lives

`src/lib/reconciler-rules/stuck-in-stage.ts:175-230` (the `act` method) makes a fetch call but does not appear to inspect or log the response status/body. If the action route returned non-200 (e.g., transient race in `agent-launcher.isAgentActive`, missing/empty `epicTitle`, or some other validation), the rule would still record the action as fired in `recentActions` even though no agent launched.

Hypotheses to verify:
1. **Stale agent-active check.** At 22:43:37, the prior test-spec session may have been mid-cleanup (lingering pid file, lock, or tmux remnant). `agent-launcher.ts` has an `isAgentActive` check that could have returned true → action endpoint returned an "Agent already running" 4xx → stuck-in-stage's fetch resolves with non-2xx but no error path catches it.
2. **Payload difference.** Stuck-in-stage's `snapshot.title` may have been empty/unexpected vs. my manual POST which used the literal epic title. The action route validates `epicTitle` is a non-empty string and returns 400 otherwise.
3. **Fetch timeout / race.** zsjv hotfix added a 15s fetch timeout (line ~216 of stuck-in-stage.ts). If the action route was slow, the rule's fetch could time out → silently logged → recentActions records the attempt regardless.

## Fix shape

Two mutually-supportive changes:

1. **Record dispatch outcome in recentActions.** The reconciler core should record the HTTP response status + body (or error) alongside `at`/`ruleName`/`epicId`/`idempotencyKey`. Today the model conflates "fetch sent" with "action accepted." Splitting these two states makes silent failures observable.

2. **stuck-in-stage logs the response.** Even without core changes, the rule's `act()` could `console.warn` non-2xx responses with the request payload — so the next-dev server log surfaces the failure for ops debugging.

## Acceptance criteria

GIVEN stuck-in-stage's act() makes a fetch to /api/fleet/action AND the response is non-2xx, WHEN the rule completes, THEN the response status + body excerpt are recorded in the reconciler's recentActions entry (or a sibling diagnostics log) AND a console.warn is emitted with the failing payload.

GIVEN the 22:43:37 niii failure scenario is replayed (test-spec stuck, agent-launcher in mid-cleanup state OR title field missing), WHEN stuck-in-stage fires, THEN the diagnostic surface clearly indicates whether the failure was a 4xx (validation/race) or 5xx (server error) or timeout — not a silent green-fire.

GIVEN a successful dispatch, WHEN the rule completes, THEN the diagnostic surface confirms 200 + tmuxSessionName, providing positive verification.

## Why P3

Not blocking: the rule fires on a 15-min cadence, so a single failed fire delays recovery by 15 min, not forever. The next window will retry. But repeated silent failures could mask a deeper bug (e.g., an isAgentActive check that's stuck-on for a particular epic), so observability is the right shape of fix.

## Cross-reference

- Related to factory-core-sy3d (umbrella: agent marker quality) and factory-core-sy3d.1 (test-spec orphan marker — the upstream cause of niii needing stuck-in-stage rescue at all).
- Reconciler status endpoint: `GET /api/fleet/reconciler/status`.
- Source: `src/lib/reconciler-rules/stuck-in-stage.ts:175-230`.

title: [FEATURE] Populate pipeline-routes CTAs for all stages (B5 deferred scope)
description:
**Source:** Pre-mortem memo `docs/research/pre-mortem-pipeline-readiness-2026-05-01.md` § 3 IF7 (lines 310-342).

## What breaks

When operator views an epic at `pipeline:research` or `pipeline:product-spec` or `pipeline:architecture`, the FleetCard renders **zero CTAs** (except stage-agnostic actions like `deprioritise`, `stop-agent`). Operator can't click "Run PM" or "Run Architect" from the dashboard — must use `curl` or manual bd commands.

## Root cause

`pipeline-routes.ts` lines 219-223 seed CTAs only for `submission-prep` stage (B2 minimal scope). All other stages have `ctas: {}` (empty object) or `ctas: undefined`. `getCTAsForStage(stage, shipType)` returns `[]` for these stages (line 250). FleetCard sees `[]` → renders no CTAs.

## The fix

Populate `PIPELINE_ROUTES[shipType].ctas[stage]` for all stages. Example (memo lines 321-337):

```typescript
"ios-app": {
  stages: [...],
  autoChain: {...},
  ctas: {
    research: ["start-research", "more-research"],
    "research-complete": ["run-pm"],
    "product-spec": ["run-architect", "revise-spec"],
    architecture: ["generate-plan", "revise-architecture"],
    "plan-review": ["approve-plan", "approve-and-build"],
    // ... etc
  },
  closureChecklistId: "ios-app",
}
```

8 ship types × 10+ stages = 80+ CTA entries.

## Files

- src/lib/pipeline-routes.ts

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All stages for all 8 ship types have `ctas` entries populated.

2. Dashboard FleetCard renders at least 1 CTA for every stage (except terminal stages like `live`).

3. All existing tests pass.

4. Marker written LAST before commit (per `standards/generic/marker-protocol.md` lines 44-58 operator directive 2026-05-01).

## Note

**Deferred scope (B5).** 373o Wave 2 (B2) seeded CTAs only for `submission-prep` to prove routing infrastructure works. Full population deferred to Wave 3. This bead is that Wave 3 work.

**Operational workaround exists:** Operator uses `/api/fleet/action` directly (see CF5 workaround). Dashboard is the primary operator interface, but CLI workaround is functional. UX degradation, not a blocker.

**Critical research gap addressed by separate bead:** `beads_web-ejr` (CF5) ships `start-research` action, which is the CRITICAL gap. This bead (IF7) ships the full CTA population for all stages — nice-to-have.

title: C1 — Internal ship-type close routing fix (stall → deploying)
description:

Phase 0 diagnostic surfaced that the bug affects **4 ship types**, not just internal: `internal`, `web-app`, `python-tool`, and `game` — all DEPLOY_TAIL ship types route incorrectly. The fix (wire up the existing dead `nextStage()` function in `pipeline-router.ts:179-195`) is the same 1-line change that corrects all 4 simultaneously. Scope expanded by coincidence-of-fix, not by design. `wordpress-plugin` is correct today only by accident (its hard-coded `submission-prep` happens to match `SUBMISSION_TAIL_AUTO_CHAIN`); the fix makes its correctness explicit.

title: F2 — Registry backup-before-write in repo-config.ts
description:
**Rationale:** Advances AC F (Operational hygiene) — "Backup-before-write on shared config so any future class-bug is recoverable." The 44-repo registry wipe on 2026-04-29 destroyed operator config and took manual recovery. Adding backup-before-write makes registry corruption recoverable in seconds.

**Source:** `docs/aspirational-pipeline/PHASE-2-PLAN-v2.md` lines 74–78 (Wave 2 item F2). AC F from `docs/aspirational-pipeline/PROBLEMS-AND-ACs.md` line 60.

**Design source-of-truth:** `factory-core/docs/research/u67-registry-backup-investigation.md` (architect memo, commit `19c7494`, 2026-05-01). All 3 design questions resolved with 0 operator BLOCKERs.

## Acceptance criteria (sharpened from architect memo § 6 — replaces sketch ACs)

1. **Backup-before-write logic in `writeConfig`** (`src/lib/repo-config.ts:39`): on entry, check if `~/.beads-web.json` exists → generate compact ISO timestamp `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ` (e.g. `20260501T034600Z`) → `fs.copyFile(CONFIG_PATH, CONFIG_PATH + '.bak.' + ts)` → if copy throws, abort write and re-throw → otherwise proceed to `fs.writeFile` → finally invoke pruning step (best-effort).

2. **Pruning logic:** after a successful write, enumerate `~/.beads-web.json.bak.*` via `fs.readdir(homedir)`, lexical-sort filenames, keep last 5, `fs.unlink` the rest. Pruning failures are logged (`console.warn`) but do NOT throw — best-effort policy so a single backup doesn't block the next one.

3. **Backup filename format guard:** filename matches regex `^\.beads-web\.json\.bak\.\d{8}T\d{6}Z$`. Unit test asserts the regex matches a generated-and-written backup name.

4. **Error handling on backup failure:** if `fs.copyFile` throws (any error class — ENOSPC / EACCES / EIO / etc.), `writeConfig` throws a wrapped Error with original cause, and `fs.writeFile` is NEVER called (existing registry preserved). Unit test mocks `fs.copyFile` to throw, asserts `fs.writeFile` is not called, asserts thrown error message names the failed-backup root cause.

5. **First-run bootstrap:** if `~/.beads-web.json` does not exist (first run, env-seed path), `fs.copyFile` is NOT called and `writeConfig` proceeds straight to `fs.writeFile`. Unit test mocks `existsSync` returning false, asserts `fs.copyFile` is not called.

6. **Caller regression check:** all 6 `writeConfig` callers in `repo-config.ts` continue to work without per-caller modification — the backup logic lives entirely inside `writeConfig`. Verified via existing `__tests__/lib/repo-config.test.ts` regression run (assert 0 new failures vs pre-edit baseline).

7. **Manual closeout verification:** trigger 7 consecutive writes via `setActiveRepo` toggling between two registered repos. Verify exactly 5 backup files remain after writes 5/6/7 (oldest pruned each time). Verify backup filenames are distinct + chronologically ordered. Verify each backup contains valid JSON parseable as `RepoStore`. Record `ls -la ~/.beads-web.json.bak.*` before + after in marker `surprises_or_findings`.

## Files (verified 2026-05-01)

- **MODIFY** `beads_web/src/lib/repo-config.ts` — `writeConfig` at line 39-41; add backup-before-write + pruning helpers internally.
- **MODIFY** `beads_web/__tests__/lib/repo-config.test.ts` — add new describe block for backup-before-write covering ACs 3, 4, 5, 6 (4-6 new test cases).

**No new files.** Backup helpers are private to `repo-config.ts`. Pattern matches existing `dolt-lifecycle.ts` style (one cohesive module).

## Architect-resolved decisions (footer)

- **Q1 (backup location):** Same-directory pattern `~/.beads-web.json.bak.<timestamp>`. Matches PHASE-2-PLAN-v2.md spec; eases recovery (`mv ~/.beads-web.json.bak.<ts> ~/.beads-web.json`); operator already has 3 ad-hoc backups in `~/` with this pattern (memo § 2).
- **Q2 (timestamp format):** Compact basic ISO `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ` (no colons, no millis). Filesystem-safe (avoids macOS Finder colon-as-slash); lexical sort is chronological; consistent with operator's existing ad-hoc backup naming (memo § 3).
- **Q3 (error handling):** Abort on backup failure — preserve existing registry, throw wrapped error, never call `fs.writeFile`. Honors AC F intent ("backup-before-write so recoverable"); fail-safe over best-effort (memo § 4).

## Phase 0 verification footer

- **FYI 1:** `writeConfig` has 6 callers (not 5 as initially estimated): `getRepos` env-seed (line 56), `addRepo` (118), `removeRepo` (134), `setActiveRepo` × 2 paths (241 + 252), `setWatchDirs` (274), `scanWatchDirs` (325). Single-point modification at `writeConfig` covers all 6 — no per-caller edits needed.
- **FYI 2:** No existing `writeConfig` test coverage (verified: grep `writeConfig` in `__tests__/lib/repo-config.test.ts` returns 0 hits). F2 adds first test coverage for this function — secondary hygiene benefit.
- **FYI 3 (atomicity, OUT OF SCOPE):** `fs.writeFile` is not atomic on POSIX. F2 makes wipe recoverable but does not prevent mid-write corruption. Atomicity (write-to-temp + rename) recommended as separate P4 follow-up bead IF a corruption incident occurs in production. Not filed yet — wait for evidence.
- **FYI 4 (no bypass env var, YAGNI):** Tests use mocked `fs` — no real backup files created during test runs. `BEADS_WEB_NO_BACKUP` would be a footgun with no use case. Architect explicitly rejected.
- **FYI 5 (operator already practices manual backup):** `~/.beads-web.json.bak-k7gy-11`, `~/.beads-web.json.bak.pre-rename-20260430-154453`, `~/.beads-web.json.bak.wipe-recovery-2026-04-29` already exist. F2 systematizes existing practice; pruning logic must NOT touch these (regex guards against pre-existing names — only files matching the strict format are eligible for pruning).

## Effort estimate

~1 hour (backup logic ~10 lines, pruning logic ~5 lines, 4-6 test cases ~30 min, manual closeout ~10 min).

## Cross-repo note

Bead filed in beads_web bd (code lives there). Tracked under umbrella `factory-core-a3ee` via `epic:factory-core-a3ee` label (no `--parent` — single-bd limitation). See `factory-core-niii` for auto-close cascade caveat.
